title: Odin: The Price of Wisdom
subtitle: One eye in a well, nine nights on a tree — knowledge is never free

learningObjectives.text: What does Odin give for wisdom?
How does he win the runes?

mimer.author: Snorri Sturluson
mimer.locator: Mimer's Well in Gylfaginning; local text normalized characters 72397-72633
mimer.excerpt: The owner of the well hight Mimer. He is full of wisdom, for he drinks from the well with the Gjallar-horn. Alfather once came there and asked for a drink from the well, but he did not get it before he left one of his eyes as a pledge.
mimer.note: Verbatim Rasmus B. Anderson translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

runes.author: Anonymous Old Norse poets
runes.locator: Havamal, stanzas 139-140; local text normalized characters 102346-102711
runes.excerpt: 139. I ween that I hung | on the windy tree, Hung there for nights full nine; With the spear I was wounded, | and offered I was To Othin, myself to myself, On the tree that none | may ever know What root beneath it runs. 140. None made me happy | with loaf or horn, And there below I looked; I took up the runes, | shrieking I took them, And forthwith back I fell.
runes.note: Verbatim Henry Adams Bellows translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

narrativeBlocks.title: One eye for a drink
narrativeBlocks.body: Mimir's well holds wisdom itself, and its keeper will share it only at a price. Odin pays with an eye — dropped into the well, where it stays. From then on the wisest god sees the world through one.

narrativeBlocks.title: Nine nights on the tree
narrativeBlocks.body: For the runes — the sacred letters that carry magic and knowledge — Odin performs a self-sacrifice: hanging nine nights on the world-tree Yggdrasil, wounded by his own spear, offering himself to himself. No food, no drink, nobody's help.

narrativeBlocks.title: He takes the runes screaming
narrativeBlocks.body: At the end of the ordeal, wisdom arrives: he looks down, sees the runes below, and seizes them. The price of the knowledge is the suffering itself — it cannot be shortcut.

narrativeBlocks.title: The wanderer-god
narrativeBlocks.body: Odin is not a thunderbolt king — he walks the world in a grey cloak and broad hat, trading small favours for news. Kings have had their hall conversations with him without ever knowing who sat at their fire.

narrativeBlocks.title: Wisdom that still costs
narrativeBlocks.body: Every knowledge-gain in Norse myth is paid for — an eye, nine nights, a hand. Watch for the pattern: in this tradition, the universe keeps accounts.

quiz.prompt: What does Odin pay for a drink from Mimir's well?

choices.text: One of his eyes — left in the well as a pledge for wisdom

quiz.explanation: The well's price is permanent: wisdom bought with sight.

quiz.prompt: How does Odin win the runes?

choices.text: By hanging nine nights wounded on Yggdrasil — a self-sacrifice that finally reveals them
By stealing them from a giant's hall
By deciphering them on the tree's bark
By trading an eye to the dwarves

quiz.explanation: The runes are won through ordeal, not study — the suffering is the purchase.
